description: A research grant proposal: persuasive, feasible and compliant with the call.
goal: Make the proposal compelling, feasible and compliant with every requirement of the call.
note: Judge the proposal against the call's criteria; aims, methods, timeline and budget must agree everywhere they appear.

readers.persona: an intelligent nonspecialist (committee member or panel generalist) who needs the significance, the main idea and the conclusions to be clear without specialist knowledge
a specialist panel reviewer who scores significance, innovation, approach and feasibility, and looks for weaknesses in the methods, timeline and preliminary evidence

reviewers.focus: compliance with the venue's or call's requirements: page or word limits, template and formatting, anonymization for double-anonymous review, required sections and statements (limitations, ethics, broader impact, reproducibility or data availability checklists, funding, conflicts), reference style and supplementary material rules

novelty and significance relative to the closest prior work: what is new, why it matters, whether the related work section positions the contribution accurately and fairly, and whether the paper explains what the reader can now do that they could not before
for proposals: whether aims, methods, timeline, team, resources and budget are consistent and achievable, whether preliminary evidence supports feasibility, and whether risks have alternatives

calibration and coherence of claims: no overclaiming (unsupported superlatives, 'prove' for empirical results, 'state of the art' without dated evidence, generalizing beyond the evidence) and no underselling (stacked hedges, buried or vague contributions); every contribution stated in the abstract and introduction is supported by specific evidence in the body and restated consistently in the discussion and conclusion; limitations are honest; numbers and claims agree everywhere they appear

every reference is real and correctly described: verify authors, title, venue, year and identifier (DOI, arXiv id, ISBN or publisher page) with web search and the citation checker; flag any reference that cannot be found as a blocker; check that each cited work actually supports the sentence citing it, that primary sources are cited, and that essential related work is not missing

fluency and coherence: paragraph flow and transitions, one idea per paragraph, consistent terminology, no repetitive wording or formulaic transitions, correct hyphens, en dashes and em dashes, no chains of 'and', parallel lists, sentence variety, concision, and American or British spelling used consistently as configured

editors.focus: prose: clarity, concision, flow between sentences and paragraphs, terminology, punctuation including hyphens and dashes, parallel lists; remove filler, formulaic transitions and repetition without removing substance or adding claims

notation, terminology and spelling across the document and against the glossary; numbers, names and claims identical wherever repeated (abstract, introduction, body, conclusion); labels, cross-references, captions, citation and reference formatting
